=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text data "3 -1 4 1 5 9 2"
text tshuf "shuffles: "
global vals long 8
global seed ulong 1
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emiti writes a signed n; the magnitude is taken as a ulong so the minimum long cannot overflow
fn emiti n long to void
if lt n 0
emit minus
emitu add bitcast ulong not n 1
else
emitu ulong n
end
end
note parse reads the decimal numbers in s (separated by spaces, an optional - sign) into vals and
note returns how many; one pass over s, so the loop is bounded by len s
fn parse s view uchar * to ulong
n = ulong 0
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
for i ulong len s
c = get s i
if eq c 45
sg = long -1
else
if and ge c 48 le c 57
v = add mul v 10 long sub c 48
dig = true
else
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
end
end
end
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
ret n
end
note show writes vals[0..n-1] separated by spaces, then a newline
fn show n ulong to void
for i ulong n
if gt i 0
emit sp
end
emiti get vals i
end
emit nl
end
note rnd is Knuth's MMIX linear congruential generator, x = x*6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
note mod 2^64 (ulong arithmetic wraps), starting from seed 0; it returns the top 31 bits, x >> 33
fn rnd to ulong
x = add mul get seed 0 6364136223846793005 1442695040888963407
put seed 0 x
ret shr x 33
end
note shuffle is Fisher-Yates: for i = n-1 .. 1 swap vals[i] with vals[rnd mod (i+1)]
fn shuffle n ulong to void
for x ulong sub n 1
i = sub sub n x 1
j = rem rnd add i 1
t = get vals i
put vals i get vals j
put vals j t
end
end
fn inorder n ulong to bool
for i ulong sub n 1
if gt get vals i get vals add i 1
ret false
end
end
ret true
end
note bgsort shuffles until sorted; with this generator and input it takes the count printed, well under
note the bound of 200000 (7! = 5040 orders, so a working generator lands far inside it)
fn bgsort n ulong to ulong
c = ulong 0
while not inorder n bound 200000
shuffle n
c = add c 1
end
ret c
end
fn main to int
n = parse data
show n
c = bgsort n
show n
emit tshuf
emitu c
emit nl
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
3 -1 4 1 5 9 2
-1 1 2 3 4 5 9
shuffles: 2314
</pre>
